Quick Read

Vivek Arya's Bank of America note that memory supply deals now run between 3 and 5 years lifted Micron 4% and Western Digital 5%.

The Roundhill Memory ETF gained 4% while the S&P 500 rose just 1%, marking this as a sector-specific rally.

Memory customer contracts stretching from under one year to three-to-five years could smooth Micron's historically punishing pricing swings.

Just released. Our analysts combed the entire stock market and named the ten best stocks to buy right now, and Micron Technology didn't make the cut. Enter your email to see the names that beat MU. The report is free. Enter your email and see if any of your stocks made the cut.

A Bank of America note arguing that memory customers are now locking in supply for years at a time is lifting chip and storage stocks together, and the group is beating the S&P 500 by a wide margin. Shares of Micron Technology (NASDAQ:MU) are at $913.77, up 4% so far in the session. The move rewards the argument that longer contracts can steady one of the most cyclical corners of the chip industry.

thinkstock

Meanwhile, Western Digital (NASDAQ:WDC) shares are at $362.32, up 5%, the largest gain in the group and a step ahead of Micron stock. SanDisk (NASDAQ:SNDK) stock is at $1,271.99, up 3%, trailing Micron stock while still joining the advance. Hard drive and flash storage names often move with memory chip makers, since the same AI data center expansion feeds demand for all three businesses and shapes how customers plan purchases.

For a sector-level check, the Roundhill Memory ETF (CBOE:DRAM) is at $48.91, up 4%, moving almost in tandem with Micron shares. The SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSEARCA:SPY) is at $764.93, up 0.65%, a much smaller gain that leaves memory and storage stocks far out in front of everything else. That gap marks this as a sector-specific rally powered by memory's own news, with the rest of the market following at a slower pace.

title: Accelevation's SkyBridge bookings strengthen Bank of America's bullish outlook
detail:
Accelevation's SkyBridge bookings strengthen Bank of America's bullish outlook
Proactive
Mon, October 26, 2026 at 12:54 PM EDT 2 min read
BAC
Trade BAC on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Accelevation's SkyBridge bookings strengthen Bank of America's bullish outlook Proactive uses images sourced from Shutterstock

Bank of America has initiated coverage of Accelevation, a data centre equipment manufacturer, with a 'buy' rating and a $20 price target, citing strong demand for power infrastructure and modular products.

The bank expects adjusted earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) to grow at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 56% between 2026 and 2030, driven by rising investment in artificial intelligence infrastructure.

Accelevation generates all its revenue from US data centres, positioning it to benefit from the expansion of facilities required to support increasingly computing-intensive AI applications.

Its 800-plus field service employees, around a quarter of whom are electricians, provide a competitive advantage as the industry faces a shortage of skilled labour.

The company also operates a fully domestic, vertically integrated manufacturing footprint, which Bank of America expects to support shorter delivery times.

Accelevation's expansion into modular equipment offers another growth opportunity, with its SkyBridge platform securing approximately $700 million in bookings in less than nine months after development began.

The bank forecasts the market for modular data centre equipment will expand at a 30% CAGR through 2030.

However, Accelevation faces execution risks as it ramps up production capacity, having completed approximately 1.1 million square feet of a planned 1.4 million-square-foot manufacturing footprint.

The expansion could temporarily weigh on margins, while additional capacity being added by competitors raises the risk that industry supply could eventually exceed demand.

Bank of America forecasts a net debt to EBITDA of 2.7 times at the end of 2026, a higher level than peers, although it expects leverage to decline rapidly.

The $20 price target is based on 10 times the company's forecast 2028 adjusted EBITDA, below the 14 times average multiple for peers using 2027 estimates.

Bank of America forecasts Accelevation's adjusted EBITDA will grow at a 77% CAGR between 2026 and 2028, compared with an estimated 34% average for peers.

Risks include customer concentration, with the company's two largest clients accounting for approximately 61% of 2025 revenue, alongside its limited public-market track record.

Former private equity owner Olympus Partners also retains 83% of Accelevation's voting power, giving it substantial control over corporate decisions.

Micron Rises as Bank of America Gets "Incrementally More Positive on Memory" After Executive Meetings ©TIKR
Key Takeaways

Micron shares rose after Bank of America's Vivek Arya kept his Buy rating and $1,550 price target following meetings with Micron's executives, and SK hynix rose [3%] too.

Customer deals that now run three to five years give this memory upcycle a better chance of outlasting past booms.

Analysts expect Micron's revenue to keep climbing through fiscal 2028, though the long-term deals cover only a little over a third of its sales.

The stock still trades as if the boom will end soon, and Micron's December report is the next big test.

Micron Technology (MU:NASDAQ) is up 2% this morning after Bank of America semiconductor analyst Vivek Arya met with its executives and came away "incrementally more positive on memory."

Arya kept his Buy rating and $1,550 price target, 77% above Friday's close. SK hynix (SKHY:NASDAQ) rose 3% too, with cash news of its own.

The contracts keep getting longer

Customer deals for memory now run three to five years, Arya's note says, where they used to last a year or less. Micron is already discussing supply for 2031.

That matters, because memory has always been boom and bust. Micron's revenue slid from $30.4 billion in fiscal 2018 to $21.4 billion in fiscal 2020, then halved in fiscal 2023…

Micron Technology (MU): total revenues, $ billions, fiscal 2017–2026 (years to August) (TIKR)

The deals commit customers to set volumes, at floor prices that management expects to deliver margins above any past cycle's peak. Micron has signed 26, covering over 35% of revenue through 2030, and it's aiming for about half.

Analysts expect revenue to keep climbing, from $133 billion in fiscal 2026 to $319 billion in fiscal 2028…

Micron Technology (MU): revenue, actual and consensus estimates, $ billions, fiscal 2024–2028 (years to August) (TIKR)

Nothing in Arya's note suggests those estimates should come down.

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Micron, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Micron's Analyst Ratings

Cash, and lots of it

Arya also estimates Micron could generate $150 billion to $200 billion of free cash flow a year in 2027 and 2028, well over double fiscal 2026's $59.0 billion. Its new buyback, up to $35.2 billion, can start on Dec. 9.

SK hynix may hand back some of its own windfall. [Dong-A Ilbo](LINK NEEDED) reported Monday that it plans a special dividend of about ₩16 trillion (about $12 billion) from the sale of its Kioxia stake. SK hynix said in a filing that nothing's decided, but it's reviewing ways to return cash and will announce them with its third-quarter results on Oct. 28.

Amazon.com (AMZN) is expected to deliver upside to Q3 Amazon Web Services growth estimates, driven by new capacity, price increases, ramping AI Lab contracts and rising enterprise inference demand, BofA Securities said.

The company is scheduled to report Q3 results Thursday after market close.

BofA said in a Sunday note that it expects revenue and earnings before interest and taxes of $202 billion and $26.4 billion, respectively, compared with Street consensus of $202.2 billion and $26.1 billion. It models AWS growth of 40% versus the Street estimate of 38%.

The investment firm expects AWS margins to remain stable at 39% in Q3, as higher depreciation is offset by strong utilization, increasing Trainium workloads, Bedrock growth and higher fees.

Declining quarter-to-date online retail spending remains a risk in Q4, but BofA forecasts revenue of $239 billion to $246 billion, compared with the Street consensus of $244.6 billion.

BofA kept a buy rating on Amazon, with a price target of $320.

title: Citigroup Lifts 2026 RoTCE Outlook: What's Fueling the Optimism?
detail:
Citigroup Lifts 2026 RoTCE Outlook: What's Fueling the Optimism?
Riya Anand
Mon, October 26, 2026 at 10:14 AM EDT 3 min read
C
BAC
CFG
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Citigroup Inc. C raised its 2026 return on tangible common equity (RoTCE) outlook to above 11% from the earlier mentioned 10-11%, reflecting improving profitability, broad-based revenue growth and progress in its transformation initiatives. The upward revision follows a solid third-quarter performance, supported by strong business momentum and improving operating efficiency. In the third quarter of 2026, Citigroup reported an RoTCE of 11.5%, up 350 basis points (bps) year over year, although the comparison benefited partly from a goodwill impairment recorded in the prior-year period.

Citigroup's improving profitability is primarily driven by strong performances across its core businesses. In the third quarter, Services revenues increased 15% year over year to $6.6 billion, aided by higher deposit balances, improved deposit spreads and fee growth. The segment delivered an impressive RoTCE of 31.2%, underscoring its importance as a key profitability driver. Wealth revenues also jumped 15% to $3.3 billion, supported by robust investment activity, while Markets and Banking revenues increased 6% each. Continued momentum across these businesses should support revenue diversification and higher returns.

Citigroup's ongoing restructuring and simplification initiatives are gradually translating into improved operating efficiency. Third-quarter operating expenses declined 2% year over year to $14 billion, although they increased 3% excluding the prior-year goodwill impairment. Nevertheless, the efficiency ratio improved to 58.5% from 64.7% a year earlier, reflecting better operating leverage. Continued investments in technology, automation and process simplification, along with progress on the Banamex divestiture, should help streamline operations and enhance profitability over time.

Nonetheless, elevated transformation-related costs, regulatory requirements and execution risks associated with restructuring remain potential headwinds. Sustaining revenue growth while containing expenses will be crucial for achieving the company's longer-term profitability targets.

Overall, Citigroup's upwardly revised RoTCE outlook signals that its multi-year turnaround is gaining traction. Strong momentum in higher-returning businesses, improving operating efficiency and disciplined capital allocation are strengthening its profitability trajectory. While execution challenges persist, continued progress on simplification initiatives and expense discipline should position Citigroup to achieve its RoTCE target of 11-13% in 2027-2028 and move closer to its medium-term goal of 14-15%.
